(1) Pro-rata allocation is a CME interest-rate-futures rule; NSE and MCX match price-time (FIFO), so inflating order size buys no extra fills. (2) Market making needs tick-level L2/L3 history and sub-second order refresh; this system has 30-second ticks, a retail Kotak API, and no stored depth history, so no honest backtest exists. (3) Passive two-sided quoting holds unhedged inventory with no stop, which the no-trade-without-SL rule forbids. (4) Spread capture is eaten by the 0.8% round-trip cost model. Registered as not applicable; the one testable piece is spun out as B-366. |
